Dear Secretary Reese:

         Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act, as amended (“FPA”) 1 and Sections 35.12
and 385.205 of the regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the
“Commission”), 2 San Gabriel Project I LLC (“Gabriel I”) submits for filing the Co-Tenancy and
Shared Facilities Agreement (“SFA”) by and among Gabriel I, San Gabriel Project II LLC
(“Gabriel II”), San Gabriel Project III LLC (“Gabriel III”), San Gabriel Project IV LLC (“Gabriel
IV”) (together, the “Co-Tenants”, and, individually, each a “Co-Tenant”), and Aypa Power
Enterprise LLC (“Manager”). Gabriel I respectfully requests that the Commission accept the SFA
for filing to become effective November 18, 2026, 61 days after the date of this filing. 3

         The SFA 4 sets forth the terms and conditions pursuant to which: (i) Gabriel I and Gabriel
II will design, install and construct, and will collectively own, operate, and maintain as tenants-in-
common a shared main power transformer and associated facilities (the “Gabriel I/II Shared
Facilities”); (ii) Gabriel III and Gabriel IV will design, install and construct, and will collectively

own, operate, and maintain as tenants-in-common a shared main power transformer and associated
facilities (the “Gabriel III/IV Shared Facilities”); and (iii) Co-Tenants will design, install and
construct, and will collectively own, operate, and maintain as tenants-in-common certain limited
interconnection facilities necessary to connect the Gabriel I/II Shared Facilities and Gabriel III/IV
Shared Facilities, and by extension Gabriel I’s battery energy storage facility (“Gabriel I Project”),
Gabriel II’s battery energy storage facility (“Gabriel II Project”), Gabriel III’s battery energy
storage facility (“Gabriel III Project”), and Gabriel IV’s battery energy storage facility (“Gabriel
IV Project”) to a point of interconnection with the transmission system owned by Southern
California Edison Company (“SCE”) (the “All Projects Shared Facilities”, which together with the
Gabriel I/II Shared Facilities and Gabriel III/IV Shared Facilities constitute the “Shared
Facilities”). Under the SFA, Manager will provide certain limited services to be performed at the
direction of the Co-Tenants with respect to the Shared Premises and Shared Facilities. Manager
will have no ownership in or control over the Shared Facilities. 5

        The SFA does not establish rates, terms, or conditions for the provision of FERC-
jurisdictional interconnection or transmission service by Co-Tenants amongst each other. The SFA
provides only for the transfer of an undivided ownership interest in the Shared Facilities and the
allocation of the costs and responsibilities of managing, operating, and maintaining the Shared
Facilities based upon each Co-Tenant’s interest in the Shared Facilities and the duties assigned to
the Manager under the SFA. Gabriel I submits the SFA for filing pursuant to Section 6.7.3 of the
SFA and Section 205 of the FPA based on the Commission’s finding that “[a]greements
concerning joint ownership of transmission facilities are . . . jurisdictional and must be filed for
Commission review,” 6 and its acceptance of similar shared facilities agreements. 7

      I.    DESCRIPTION OF PARTIES AND THE SFA

       A. Parties

      Gabriel I is a Delaware limited liability company formed for the purposes of developing,
owning, and operating the Gabriel I Project. The Gabriel I Project will be an approximately 125

        Gabriel III is a Delaware limited liability company formed for the purposes of developing,

        Gabriel IV is a Delaware limited liability company formed for the purposes of developing,

           B. The SFA

        The SFA sets forth the terms and conditions pursuant to which the Co-Tenants will own an
interest in the Shared Facilities in proportion to each Co-Tenant’s Pro Rata Share as set forth in
Exhibit B of the SFA. 9 The SFA also requires the Co-Tenants to comply with the terms and
conditions of certain shared premises agreements to facilitate the construction, ownership, and
operation of their respective Facilities and the Shared Facilities. 10

        Each Co-Tenant shall have the right to use the Shared Facilities to the extent of its
Undivided Interest in the Shared Facilities and consistent with the terms of the SFA. A Co-Tenant’s
use of the Shared Facilities may not interfere with any other Co-Tenant’s use and enjoyment of
the Shared Facilities or the operation of its Facilities. 11 No Co-Tenant may use or permit the use
of the Shared Facilities in any manner that (i) has an adverse effect on any other Co-Tenant, other
than as contemplated in the SFA, (ii) interferes with the use of the Shared Facilities by any other
Co-Tenant, or (iii) jeopardizes the issuance or maintenance of any insurance policy relating to the
Shared Assets or any governmental approval as to the Shared Facilities or any other Co-Tenant’s
Facilities. 12 The SFA includes limits on how and when a Co-Tenant may install Additional
Facilities or interconnect its Facilities so as not to interfere with the other Co-Tenants’ use of the
Shared Facilities. 13 Each Co-Tenant shall be responsible for and shall make payment to Manager
for Shared Expenses (including taxes) arising from and after the Election Date in proportion to its
Percentage Interest. 14

     III.       INFORMATION REQUIRED BY 18 C.F.R. PART 35

       This is an initial rate schedule filing. As such, Gabriel I submits the following information
required by Section 35.12 of the Commission’s regulations:

        A. List of Documents Submitted with the Filing (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(a))

            This filing consists of:

                     (i)    This transmittal letter; and

                     (ii)   Attachment A - the SFA.

        B. Effective Date (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(a))



15

       Gabriel I requests that the Commission make the SFA effective as of November 18, 2026,
61 days after filing.

      C. Persons to Whom the Rate Schedule Has Been Mailed (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(a))

      The Co-Tenants and the Manager are the only parties to the SFA. As such, the Co-Tenants
and Manager have not mailed copies of this filing to any other parties.

      D. Description of the Rate Schedule (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(a))

       See Part I.B above.

      E. All Requisite Agreement Has Been Obtained (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(a))

      The Co-Tenants have no similar arrangements with other parties to which they could
compare rates.

      F. Estimates of Transactions and Revenues (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(b)(1))

        The Co-Tenants will not be charging each other for any FERC-jurisdictional service under
the terms of the SFA. Instead, the SFA establishes a framework for the Co-Tenants to share the
costs incurred in connection with the operation and maintenance of the Shared Facilities.

      G. Comparison of Rates (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(b)(3))

      The Co-Tenants have no similar arrangements with other parties to which they could
compare rates.

      H. Facilities Installed or Modified (18 C.F.R. § 35.12(b)(4))

       The Shared Facilities subject to the SFA are described in Exhibit A-1 of the SFA.

      I. Request for Waiver of Requirements to Provide Additional Information

        Gabriel I respectfully requests waiver of the requirements to provide additional information
under 18 C.F.R. § 35.12 beyond the information provided above because the SFA provides for the
Co-Tenants to share the actual costs of operating and maintaining the Shared Facilities on the basis
of their interests in the Shared Facilities and does not establish any rates for Commission-
jurisdictional interconnection or transmission service. Each Co-Tenant will own and use only that
portion of the Shared Facilities necessary to interconnect its generating facility to the SCE
transmission grid.
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese
September 18, 2026
Page 7


    IV.      CONCLUSION

       For the foregoing reasons, Gabriel I respectfully requests that the Commission accept the
SFA for filing, without modification or condition, with an effective date of November 18, 2026,
and grant the waivers requested herein.

                             CO-TENANCY AND SHARED FACILITIES AGREEMENT

                    THIS CO-TENANCY AND SHARED FACILITIES AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”)
            is entered into as of August 11, 2026 (the “Effective Date”), by and among San Gabriel Project I
            LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Gabriel I”), San Gabriel Project II LLC, a Delaware
            limited liability company (“Gabriel II”), San Gabriel Project III LLC, a Delaware limited liability
            company (“Gabriel III”), San Gabriel Project IV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company
            (“Gabriel IV”) (the foregoing parties may be referred to from time to time herein each separately
            as a “Co-Tenant,” and collectively, as the “Co-Tenants”) and Aypa Power Enterprise LLC, a
            Delaware limited liability company (the “Manager,” and collectively with Gabriel I¸ Gabriel II,
            Gabriel III and Gabriel IV, the “Parties”, and each individually a “Party”).

                                                             RECITALS:

                    A.      Gabriel I is developing and constructing an approximately 125 MW battery energy
            storage facility located in Irwindale, CA, consisting of battery energy storage equipment and
            associated equipment, foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the
            “Gabriel I Project”).

                   B.      Gabriel II is developing an approximately 75 MW battery energy storage facility in
            Irwindale, CA that will consist of battery energy storage equipment and associated equipment,
            foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the “Gabriel II Project”).

                   C.      Gabriel III is developing an up to 100 MW battery energy storage facility in
            Irwindale, CA that will consist of battery energy storage equipment and associated equipment,
            foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the “Gabriel III Project”).

                    D.     Gabriel IV is developing an approximately 100 MW battery energy storage facility
            in Irwindale, CA that will consist of battery energy storage equipment and associated equipment,
            foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the “Gabriel IV Project”).
            Together, the Gabriel I Project, the Gabriel II Project, the Gabriel III Project and the Gabriel IV
            Project shall be referred to as the “Projects”, and may be referred to herein individually as a
            “Project”. The Projects will be constructed in proximity to one another.

                    E.     Gabriel I and Gabriel II (collectively, “Gabriel I/II Co-Tenants,” and each,
            individually, a “Gabriel I/II Co-Tenant”) will design, install and construct, and will collectively
            own, operate, and maintain, on the land described in Exhibit A-3 as the Shared Premises, a shared
            main power transformer and associated facilities, all as more particularly described in Exhibit A-
            1 (as may be updated from time to time in accordance with this Agreement the “Gabriel I/II Shared
            Facilities”).

                   F.       Gabriel III and Gabriel IV (collectively, “Gabriel III/IV Co-Tenants,” and each,
            individually, a “Gabriel III/IV Co-Tenant”) will design, install and construct, and will collectively
            own, operate, and maintain, on the land described in Exhibit A-3 as the Shared Premises, a shared
            main power transformer and associated facilities, all as more particularly described in Exhibit A-
            1 (as may be updated from time to time in accordance with this Agreement the “Gabriel III/IV
            Shared Facilities”).
 Docusign Envelope ID: AED87DAC-C3B7-8DD6-81AE-FA6BA419CFE5




                   G.      The Co-Tenants will design, install and construct, and will collectively own,
            operate, and maintain, on the land described in Exhibit A-3 as the Shared Premises and within the
            Co-Tenants’ 230 kV/34.5 kV substation, the high-voltage buswork, switching, foundations, relay,
            and breaker equipment and other facilities connecting to and the point of interconnection with the
            transmission system owned by Southern California Edison Company (“Transmission Provider”),
            all as more particularly described in Exhibit A-1 (as may be updated from time to time in
            accordance with this Agreement, the “All Projects Shared Facilities”).

                    H.    The Shared Facilities will be constructed according to that certain Large Generation
            Interconnection Agreement, dated as of June 10, 2025, among Transmission Provider, CAISO and
            San Gabriel Project LLC, for 400 MW of interconnection service for the Projects, which agreement
            San Gabriel Project LLC intends to assign to the Co-Tenants and amend to replace San Gabriel
            Project LLC with the Co-Tenants as the counterparties to Transmission Provider and CAISO (as
            amended or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Interconnection Agreement”). Manager
            and the Co-Tenants intend to enter into a co-tenancy agreement, with Manager acting as
            “Manager” thereunder, relating to the sharing of rights and responsibilities under the
            Interconnection Agreement (the “Co-Tenancy Agreement”).

                    I.     Each Co-Tenant holds certain fee, lease, easement and/or other real property
            interests pursuant to those agreements more particularly described in Exhibit A-2 (the “Shared
            Premises Agreements”), each of which permits or allows access to and use of the Shared Premises
            by the applicable Co-Tenant.

                    J.     The Co-Tenants are entering into this Agreement to provide for joint ownership
            and shared use of the Shared Facilities. The Co-Tenants wish to set forth herein their respective
            rights and obligations regarding the design, procurement, development, construction, installation,
            ownership, use, maintenance, repair, replacement of, and alterations to the Shared Facilities.

                   K.      The Co-Tenants will share in the cost of the Shared Facilities in accordance with
            the provisions of this Agreement.

                   L.      The Co-Tenants also wish to contract with the Manager for the provision of certain
            limited services to be performed at the direction of the Co-Tenants with respect to the Shared
            Premises and Shared Facilities, and the Manager wishes to accept said engagement on the terms
            and conditions contained herein.

                                                        AGREEMENT:

                    “FERC” means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission or its successor agency.

                  “FPA” shall mean the Federal Power Act, as amended, and the implementing regulations

                  “Financing Document” means an agreement entered into between a Financing Party and a

                   “Financing Party” means any Person providing direct or indirect debt, equity or tax equity
            financing, refinancing or extending credit (including any financing lease or tax equity partnership)
            to a Co-Tenant. For the purposes of this Agreement, any counterparty to a Co-Tenant in a swap,

                             CO-TENANCY AND SHARED FACILITIES AGREEMENT

                    THIS CO-TENANCY AND SHARED FACILITIES AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”)
            is entered into as of August 11, 2026 (the “Effective Date”), by and among San Gabriel Project I
            LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Gabriel I”), San Gabriel Project II LLC, a Delaware
            limited liability company (“Gabriel II”), San Gabriel Project III LLC, a Delaware limited liability
            company (“Gabriel III”), San Gabriel Project IV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company
            (“Gabriel IV”) (the foregoing parties may be referred to from time to time herein each separately
            as a “Co-Tenant,” and collectively, as the “Co-Tenants”) and Aypa Power Enterprise LLC, a
            Delaware limited liability company (the “Manager,” and collectively with Gabriel I¸ Gabriel II,
            Gabriel III and Gabriel IV, the “Parties”, and each individually a “Party”).

                                                             RECITALS:

                    A.      Gabriel I is developing and constructing an approximately 125 MW battery energy
            storage facility located in Irwindale, CA, consisting of battery energy storage equipment and
            associated equipment, foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the
            “Gabriel I Project”).

                   B.      Gabriel II is developing an approximately 75 MW battery energy storage facility in
            Irwindale, CA that will consist of battery energy storage equipment and associated equipment,
            foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the “Gabriel II Project”).

                   C.      Gabriel III is developing an up to 100 MW battery energy storage facility in
            Irwindale, CA that will consist of battery energy storage equipment and associated equipment,
            foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the “Gabriel III Project”).

                    D.     Gabriel IV is developing an approximately 100 MW battery energy storage facility
            in Irwindale, CA that will consist of battery energy storage equipment and associated equipment,
            foundations, and substation and related facilities and improvements (the “Gabriel IV Project”).
            Together, the Gabriel I Project, the Gabriel II Project, the Gabriel III Project and the Gabriel IV
            Project shall be referred to as the “Projects”, and may be referred to herein individually as a
            “Project”. The Projects will be constructed in proximity to one another.

                    E.     Gabriel I and Gabriel II (collectively, “Gabriel I/II Co-Tenants,” and each,
            individually, a “Gabriel I/II Co-Tenant”) will design, install and construct, and will collectively
            own, operate, and maintain, on the land described in Exhibit A-3 as the Shared Premises, a shared
            main power transformer and associated facilities, all as more particularly described in Exhibit A-
            1 (as may be updated from time to time in accordance with this Agreement the “Gabriel I/II Shared
            Facilities”).

                   F.       Gabriel III and Gabriel IV (collectively, “Gabriel III/IV Co-Tenants,” and each,
            individually, a “Gabriel III/IV Co-Tenant”) will design, install and construct, and will collectively
            own, operate, and maintain, on the land described in Exhibit A-3 as the Shared Premises, a shared
            main power transformer and associated facilities, all as more particularly described in Exhibit A-
            1 (as may be updated from time to time in accordance with this Agreement the “Gabriel III/IV
            Shared Facilities”).
 Docusign Envelope ID: AED87DAC-C3B7-8DD6-81AE-FA6BA419CFE5




                   G.      The Co-Tenants will design, install and construct, and will collectively own,
            operate, and maintain, on the land described in Exhibit A-3 as the Shared Premises and within the
            Co-Tenants’ 230 kV/34.5 kV substation, the high-voltage buswork, switching, foundations, relay,
            and breaker equipment and other facilities connecting to and the point of interconnection with the
            transmission system owned by Southern California Edison Company (“Transmission Provider”),
            all as more particularly described in Exhibit A-1 (as may be updated from time to time in
            accordance with this Agreement, the “All Projects Shared Facilities”).

                    H.    The Shared Facilities will be constructed according to that certain Large Generation
            Interconnection Agreement, dated as of June 10, 2025, among Transmission Provider, CAISO and
            San Gabriel Project LLC, for 400 MW of interconnection service for the Projects, which agreement
            San Gabriel Project LLC intends to assign to the Co-Tenants and amend to replace San Gabriel
            Project LLC with the Co-Tenants as the counterparties to Transmission Provider and CAISO (as
            amended or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Interconnection Agreement”). Manager
            and the Co-Tenants intend to enter into a co-tenancy agreement, with Manager acting as
            “Manager” thereunder, relating to the sharing of rights and responsibilities under the
            Interconnection Agreement (the “Co-Tenancy Agreement”).

                    I.     Each Co-Tenant holds certain fee, lease, easement and/or other real property
            interests pursuant to those agreements more particularly described in Exhibit A-2 (the “Shared
            Premises Agreements”), each of which permits or allows access to and use of the Shared Premises
            by the applicable Co-Tenant.

                    J.     The Co-Tenants are entering into this Agreement to provide for joint ownership
            and shared use of the Shared Facilities. The Co-Tenants wish to set forth herein their respective
            rights and obligations regarding the design, procurement, development, construction, installation,
            ownership, use, maintenance, repair, replacement of, and alterations to the Shared Facilities.

                   K.      The Co-Tenants will share in the cost of the Shared Facilities in accordance with
            the provisions of this Agreement.

                   L.      The Co-Tenants also wish to contract with the Manager for the provision of certain
            limited services to be performed at the direction of the Co-Tenants with respect to the Shared
            Premises and Shared Facilities, and the Manager wishes to accept said engagement on the terms
            and conditions contained herein.

                    “AAA” has the meaning set forth in Section 15.2.1.

                                                             RECITALS

                    A.      The Co-Tenants are parties to the Co-Tenancy and Shared Facilities Agreement dated as
            of the Agreement Date (the “Shared Facilities Agreement”). Capitalized terms used but not otherwise
            defined herein shall have the meaning ascribed thereto in the Shared Facilities Agreement.

                     B.       The Co-Tenants are each separately developing and will each separately construct, own
            and operate a battery energy storage facility located in Los Angeles County, California. Gabriel I’s battery
            energy storage facility and related infrastructure (the “Gabriel I Project”) will have a capacity of
            approximately 125 MW. Gabriel II’s battery energy storage facility and related infrastructure (the “Gabriel
            II Project”) will have a capacity of up to 75 MW. Gabriel III’s battery energy storage facility and related
            infrastructure (the “Gabriel III Project”) will have a capacity of up to 100 MW. Gabriel IV’s battery energy
            storage facility and related infrastructure will have a capacity of up to 100 MW (the “Gabriel IV Project”,

                     1.      Declaration of Intention. On and subject to the terms and conditions of the Shared Facilities
            Agreement, the Co-Tenants hereby declare that the relationship of the Co-Tenants in and to the Shared
            Facilities is and shall remain that of tenants-in-common holding an Undivided Interest in each Shared
            Facilities Group equal to each such Co-Tenant’s respective Percentage Interest in the applicable Shared
            Facilities Group (as such Percentage Interest is determined pursuant to the Shared Facilities Agreement).

                     2.       Properties Benefitted and Bound. The rights and obligations of the Parties under the Shared
            Facilities Agreement benefit and burden the Shared Premises. The covenants and obligations under the
            Shared Facilities Agreement are and shall be considered covenants running with the land. All sales,
            conveyances and other transfers of a Co-Tenant’s Project, such Co-Tenant’s Percentage Interest, and/or the
            Shared Premises Agreements to which such Co-tenant is a party, shall be subject to all of the terms and
            conditions of the Shared Facilities Agreement, whether or not expressly stated in any instrument of sale,
            conveyance or transfer. The covenants, terms and provisions set forth in the Shared Facilities Agreement
            shall inure to the benefit of the Parties hereto and any other Person having any rights in the Shared Facilities
            Agreement, and their respective permitted grantees, assignees, transferees, heirs, legatees, executors,

                     3.      Incorporation; Conflicts. The terms and conditions of the Shared Facilities Agreement are
            incorporated herein by reference. This Memorandum is being executed and recorded to evidence the Shared
            Facilities Agreement and shall not be construed to limit, amend or modify the provisions of the Shared
            Facilities Agreement in any respect. In the event of any conflict between the provisions of the Shared
            Facilities Agreement and the provisions of this Memorandum, the Shared Facilities Agreement shall
            control. This Memorandum may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed
            an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one agreement.
